scheme: ALA-LC-style romanization of Persian, as pronounced in Iran
en: Bird of the dawn, raise your lament,
with a sigh that rains sparks, break this cage and turn it upside down.
Nightingale with bound wings, come out of the corner of the cage, sing the song of the freedom of humankind,
and with one breath fill the field of this heap of dust with sparks, fill it with sparks.
The tyranny of the tyrant, the cruelty of the hunter, have scattered my nest to the wind.
O God, O heaven, O nature, turn our dark night into dawn.
It is early spring, the flowers are in bloom; the cloud of my eye rains dew;
this cage, like my heart, is narrow and dark.
Cast flame into the cage, O fiery sigh;
hand of nature, do not pluck the flower of my life;
O fresh flower, look toward the lover more than this, more, more.
Heartsick bird, make the tale of separation short, make it short.
rom: ze āh-e sharar-bār in qafas rā bar-shekan o zir-o-zebar kon
bolbol-e par-baste ze konj-e qafas dar-ā naghme-ye āzādi-ye now'-e bashar sarā
v-az nafasi 'arse-ye in khāk-tude rā por-sharar kon, por-sharar kon
zolm-e zālem, jowr-e sayyād āshiyānam dāde bar bād
ey Khodā, ey falak, ey tabi'at shām-e tārik-e mā rā sahar kon
now-bahār ast, gol be-bār ast abr-e cheshmam zhāle-bār ast
in qafas, chon delam, tang o tār ast
sho'le fekan dar qafas ey āh-e ātashin
jāneb-e 'āsheq negah ey tāze gol az in bishtar kon, bishtar kon, bishtar kon
morgh-e bidel, sharh-e hejrān mokhtasar, mokhtasar kon
notes: This is the first of Bahar's two stanzas, the one sung. The second, more openly political, names the betrayers of the constitution; it is printed in the Persian Wikipedia's article but rarely performed.
The bird in the cage is the nation under despotism; the song was first sung in 1927, in the last years of the Constitutional Revolution's struggle, and has been a song of protest in Iran ever since.
